transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Elena Brooks (Redwood CSM), Samir Rao (Lithos Head of ML), Jules Park (Lithos VP Eng), Anita Gomez (Lithos Security Lead), Derek Li (Lithos Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imprecise): Discussed onboarding approach. Plan to pilot on hosted API, then consider Redwood Dedicated. Security asks include KMS, audit logs, and SSO. SE to run perf tests and return numbers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh we'll kick off in a sec, i see lithos folks on the call, can you hear me okay?
[00:07] Samir Rao: yep loud and clear, thanks maya, appreciate it.
[00:10] Maya Patel: cool. quick intro round robin, i'll hand it to carlos for the technical agenda.
[00:15] Carlos Nguyen: thanks. hi all, carlos here, i'll walk through the typical onramp, network options, and then propose a short benchmark plan. goal is to get a pilot running in two weeks.
[00:27] Jules Park: that works. our main constraints are throughput for live inference and security compliance, so both matters.
[00:34] Anita Gomez: and we have strict log retention rules, plus we need KMS integration and to verify no customer PII is retained unless encrypted.
[00:42] Maya Patel: understood. high level, we usually suggest starting hosted for fastest time-to-value, then you can move to Redwood Dedicated or Private if you need isolated capacity or on-prem.
[00:52] Samir Rao: can you remind us the tradeoffs? we saw a doc but some terms were fuzzy.
[00:58] Carlos Nguyen: sure. hosted is our managed api - lowest friction, we manage runtime, model variants, and we give metrics. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, better isolation. private is VPC or on-prem for regulated data. tradeoffs are cost and operational ownership. hosted has fastest rollout, dedicated gives SLO guarantees.
[01:18] Derek Li: when you say private, is that full on-prem or VPC peering? our ops prefers VPC peering first.
[01:24] Carlos Nguyen: both. private can mean a customer-managed VPC where control plane is private, or a full on-prem package. you can start with VPC peering to hosted control plane.
[01:33] Jules Park: what ports or egress do we need to open? network is the heavy lift for us.
[01:38] Carlos Nguyen: primarily outbound HTTPS to our API endpoints, and for VPC peering we need BGP routes and specific subnets. We'll share a network playbook. there might be a couple of ports for telemetry if you opt in to trace forwarding, but it's optional.
[01:53] Anita Gomez: we need to capture audit logs in our SIEM. is there a streaming option?
[01:58] Elena Brooks: yep, we have audit log forwarders and S3 delivery options. logs can go to your S3 bucket or to our retention layer depending on the plan. note: retention and export policies differ between hosted and dedicated.
[02:12] Samir Rao: what's the recommended route for us, given we are starting with real user queries and need latency under 200ms 95th?
[02:20] Carlos Nguyen: 200ms 95th is tight for larger models. two levers: model size and quantization, and hosting close to your region. For many customers we do a small-seq prompt optimization and prefix caching so short queries hit 80-120ms. For your throughput needs we can start hosted in a region close to you and instrument results.
[02:39] Jules Park: mic check — you mentioned cache, is that KV cache or prefix cache?
[02:43] Carlos Nguyen: both terms used. we have prefix/KV cache, automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts, and a KV cache for conversation state. sometimes transcript says K V cache, so docs may vary.
[02:55] Samir Rao: okay, and about security: SSO and KMS — can we bring our KMS?
[03:01] Maya Patel: yes, for Dedicated and Private deployments customers can bring KMS or we can integrate with customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. Hosted also supports customer-managed keys via a KMS bridge for enterprise tiers.
[03:14] Anita Gomez: can we see the SOC 2 report and your security pack? we have a vendor review checklist.
[03:19] Maya Patel: absolutely. i'll share the security pack and SOC2 summary after the call. i'll also include the redwood ded- uh 'redwood dedicate' paperwork, and the KMS integration guide.
[03:31] Derek Li: for the pilot we want to avoid heavy infra changes. is there a minimal config that gets us going?
[03:36] Carlos Nguyen: yes, minimal is hosted api with an API key and network allowlist. then we can add VPC peering on week two if you want to test Dedicated later. We'll propose a canary routing policy so traffic falls back to a smaller model when needed.
[03:50] Jules Park: sounds good. timeline?
[03:53] Maya Patel: proposal: share pricing and pilot terms by end of week (that's tuesday for us), benchmark run next week by carlos, pilot start date wednesday march 8th for two weeks, and security artifacts delivered by maya within 48 hours.
[04:10] Samir Rao: that timeline is okay; we'd like to have a short 30 minute network walkthrough with derek and carlos.
[04:16] Carlos Nguyen: happy to do that. derek, can you propose two 30 minute windows next week?
[04:21] Derek Li: i'll send via calendar, probably tuesday afternoon or thursday morning.
[04:25] Anita Gomez: one question on data retention — if we enable audit forwarding to our SIEM does any user text get stored on your side in plaintext?
[04:33] Elena Brooks: by default some telemetry stays in our logs for 30 days for troubleshooting, but for enterprise pilots we can change retention and enable encryption and masking. we can also disable transcript retention for certain routes. we'll detail options in the security pack.
[04:48] Samir Rao: perfect. on the benchmark, what metrics do you plan to return?
[04:52] Carlos Nguyen: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens-per-second, cost per token estimate, and throughput at concurrency levels you expect. i'll run using your sample corpus and a synthetic concurrency profile.
[05:04] Jules Park: our concurrency will be spiky, mostly bursts of 50-200 qps.
[05:09] Carlos Nguyen: noted. i'll stress test with bursts. also we'll try with quantized variants to show cost/loss tradeoffs.
[05:17] Maya Patel: competitors question — any reason lithos picked redwood vs bedrock or others?
[05:21] Samir Rao: we liked the production tooling, the rollout controls, and the whitepaper on cost controls. also the eval tooling looked useful.
[05:29] Maya Patel: great. last bits: deliverables recap. carlos runs benchmark and uploads sheet. maya shares security pack, pricing pilot terms. derek schedules network walkthrough. anita shares vendor checklist and retention requirements.
[05:43] Anita Gomez: i'll compile the checklist today and send it.
[05:46] Maya Patel: perfect. any other questions?
[05:49] Jules Park: none from me.
[05:51] Samir Rao: all good. thanks everyone.
[05:53] Maya Patel: thanks lithos team. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule invites. bye.

End of transcript.
